title: Prediction of MDMA response in healthy humans: A pooled analysis of placebo-controlled studies

claims.statement: In 194 healthy, screened volunteers aged 18 to 45, four in five new to MDMA, who each took one capsule of MDMA lying in a quiet hospital ward in Basel, with a placebo on another day (10 double-blind crossover studies pooled by the laboratory that ran them; 125 mg for 164 people and 75 mg for 30, the same for women and men, as study conditions; Studerus et al., 2021), the amount taken per kilogram of body weight and the resulting blood level went most with how strongly the effects were felt, as the volunteers rated them. Without adjustment, the blood level was associated with the rating of any drug effect (standardized beta 0.48), and in penalized models dose per kilogram was selected for 21 of 25 effects and ranked first for 12, mostly pleasant and stimulating ones, but mattered less for unpleasant or anxious reactions. At the same dose per kilogram, lower activity of the liver enzyme CYP2D6 went with a higher blood level (beta −0.19), older age with a smaller rise in heart rate (−0.27), higher openness with more closeness to others (0.28) and oceanic boundlessness (0.22), higher neuroticism and trait anxiety, measured at screening, with more dread of ego dissolution (0.32 each) and impaired control (0.26 each), and a more anxious-depressed or introverted mood just before the capsule with more anxiety during the session (0.25 and 0.23); each explained 5 to 12% of the variation (semi-partial R2). For a rating of a bad drug effect, older age, trait anxiety and anxious-depressed mood before the dose ranked highest. Women and men did not differ once dose per kilogram was allowed for; because everyone took a fixed amount and women weighed less, women received more per kilogram, and this design cannot separate sex from dose per kilogram. Previous MDMA use showed no association, but no one had used it more than five times. Expectations were not among the measures, and the setting, the same for everyone, could not be studied. Bodies that differ are one reason people feel more or less from the same amount; everyone took one fixed dose, so what happens when someone who feels little takes more was not tested here (controlled studies of a second dose are covered in a separate answer). Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
claims.magnitude: Unadjusted: blood level and any drug effect beta 0.48. Penalized models: dose per kilogram selected for 21 of 25 responses, first for 12. Adjusted for dose per kilogram: CYP2D6 activity and blood level −0.19 (R2 0.10); age and heart-rate rise −0.27 (R2 0.07); openness and closeness 0.28 (R2 0.08), oceanic boundlessness 0.22 (R2 0.06); neuroticism and trait anxiety and dread of ego dissolution 0.32 each (R2 0.12 and 0.11), impaired control 0.26 each; anxious-depressed and introverted mood before the dose and 5D-ASC anxiety 0.25 and 0.23 (R2 0.06 and 0.05). Sex and previous MDMA use (at most five times): no association after adjustment.
